* *

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ The exegetes said: The believers said, "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, we would do them, and we would spend our wealth and our selves in them." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure." Then they were tested by this on the day of Uhud, and they turned their backs in flight. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ [Al-Tabari transmitted several reports: 28/83-84; see also Ibn Kathir: 4/359. Al-Suyuti attributed this report in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/146 to Ibn Abi Hatim. See also al-Wahidi p. (492).]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: When Allah the Exalted informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of the reward of the martyrs of Badr, the Companions said, "If we meet battle after this, we will surely exhaust our utmost effort in it." Then they fled on the day of Uhud, and Allah rebuked them with this verse. [See al-Qurtubi: 18/78.]

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning the matter of fighting. A man would say, "I fought," when he had not fought, "I thrust," when he had not thrust, and "I struck," when he had not struck. So this verse was revealed. [Transmitted by al-Tabari: 28/84-85; mentioned by Ibn Kathir: 4/359. See also al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/261.]

Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, who used to promise victory to the believers while they were lying. [Mentioned by al-Tabari: 28/85, who gave preference, saying: "The most correct of these views regarding the interpretation of the verse is the view of those who said: it refers to those who said, 'If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would act upon them,' and then fell short in acting upon them after they had known." See also al-Bahr al-Muhit 8/261.]

﴿Very hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say﴾: the phrase is in the nominative position (fi mawdi' al-raf'), and it is like your saying, "What a man your brother is!" The meaning of the verse: that is great in hatefulness and detestation in the sight of Allah, i.e., Allah hates intensely that you say ﴿what you do not do﴾, that you promise yourselves something and then do not fulfill it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 61, verse 4–5:

﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks (ṣaffan), as if they were a solid structure.﴾ Meaning: they arrange themselves in ranks at the time of fighting, and they do not move from their positions. ﴿As if they were a solid structure﴾: it has been fitted together, one part joined to another [meaning: one part was stuck to another] and firmly set, so there is no gap or flaw in it. It is also said: "like lead."

﴿And when Moses said to his people﴾ from the Children of Israel: ﴿"O my people, why do you hurt me?"﴾ This was when they accused him of having a swelling in the testicles (al-udrah). ﴿And you know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you﴾, and a messenger is to be glorified [and honored] and respected. ﴿So when they deviated﴾, they turned away from the truth. ﴿Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾: He inclined them away from the truth. The meaning is that when they abandoned the truth by harming their prophet, Allah turned their hearts away from the truth. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: this means He does not guide those whom He has known in His knowledge to be defiant.

It has two meanings:

First: it is an intensive form of the agent (al-fa'il), meaning that all the prophets are praisers of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and he (the Prophet Muhammad) praises God more than anyone else.

Second: it is an intensive form of the object (al-maf'ul), meaning that all the prophets are praised for the commendable qualities in them, and he is [the most intensively praised] [[In manuscript "B": (the most intensively praised, with excellences)]] and the most comprehensive of the virtues and good qualities for which one is praised.

﴿So when he came to them with clear proofs, they said: "This is clear magic."﴾

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God while he is being invited to Islam? And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. They wish to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 61, verses 13–14:**

﴿And another [favour] you love﴾. That is: for you there is another quality in this world, alongside the reward of the Hereafter, that you love. That quality is: ﴿help from Allah and a near victory﴾. Al-Kalbi said: it is victory over Quraysh and the conquest of Makkah. ʿAṭāʾ said: it refers to the conquest of Persia and Rome.

﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, O Muhammad (ﷺ), of victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. Then He urged them to support the religion and to fight those who oppose it, saying: ﴿O you who believe, be helpers of Allah﴾. The people of the Ḥijāz and Abū ʿAmr recited "anṣāran" (أنصارًا) with tanwīn, and "lillāh" (لِلَّهِ) with the lām of possession. The others recited "anṣāra Allāh" (أنصار الله) as a construct phrase, in line with His saying: "We are the helpers of Allah."

﴿As Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples﴾. That is, support the religion of Allah in the way the disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn, the apostles) supported it when Jesus, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿Who are my helpers for Allah?﴾, that is: who will help me in the cause of Allah? ﴿The disciples said: We are the helpers of Allah. So a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās said: this refers to the time of Jesus, peace be upon him. When he was raised up, his people split into three groups. One group said: he was Allah, so he ascended. Another group said: he was the son of Allah, so Allah raised him to Himself. A third group said: he was the servant of Allah and His messenger, so Allah raised him to Himself, and they were the believers. Each group was followed by a section of the people, and they fought one another. The two disbelieving groups prevailed over the believers, until Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ). Then the believing group prevailed over the disbelieving one. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾, that is, they became superior and victorious.

Mughīrah narrated from Ibrāhīm, who said: "The proof of those who believed in Jesus became manifest through the confirmation of Muhammad (ﷺ) that Jesus was the Word of Allah and His Spirit."

[[Cited by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr: 8/150, attributing it to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 61, verses 13–14:**

﴿And another [favour] you love﴾. That is: for you there is another quality in this world, alongside the reward of the Hereafter, that you love. That quality is: ﴿help from Allah and a near victory﴾. Al-Kalbi said: it is victory over Quraysh and the conquest of Makkah. ʿAṭāʾ said: it refers to the conquest of Persia and Rome.

﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, O Muhammad (ﷺ), of victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. Then He urged them to support the religion and to fight those who oppose it, saying: ﴿O you who believe, be helpers of Allah﴾. The people of the Ḥijāz and Abū ʿAmr recited "anṣāran" (أنصارًا) with tanwīn, and "lillāh" (لِلَّهِ) with the lām of possession. The others recited "anṣāra Allāh" (أنصار الله) as a construct phrase, in line with His saying: "We are the helpers of Allah."

﴿As Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples﴾. That is, support the religion of Allah in the way the disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn, the apostles) supported it when Jesus, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿Who are my helpers for Allah?﴾, that is: who will help me in the cause of Allah? ﴿The disciples said: We are the helpers of Allah. So a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās said: this refers to the time of Jesus, peace be upon him. When he was raised up, his people split into three groups. One group said: he was Allah, so he ascended. Another group said: he was the son of Allah, so Allah raised him to Himself. A third group said: he was the servant of Allah and His messenger, so Allah raised him to Himself, and they were the believers. Each group was followed by a section of the people, and they fought one another. The two disbelieving groups prevailed over the believers, until Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ). Then the believing group prevailed over the disbelieving one. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾, that is, they became superior and victorious.

Mughīrah narrated from Ibrāhīm, who said: "The proof of those who believed in Jesus became manifest through the confirmation of Muhammad (ﷺ) that Jesus was the Word of Allah and His Spirit."
